_note: Everything an attendee can see is in this file. No code changes needed to rewrite the booth's voice. Run `npm run lines` after editing - it fails if any combination is missing, or if a line will not set legibly.

options.label: The one who talks to users
The one who just got here

_lines: A 5 x 6 matrix: every identity crossed with every confession. Both answers have to be visible in the result, otherwise the first question is decoration. Three lines per cell so 'try another' has somewhere to go. Keep them under about 50 characters.

friday: I ship on Fridays. That is the personality.
killed: I shipped it, then I killed it
Built it. Shipped it. Buried it.
Shipped fast enough to kill it early
graveyard: I ship fast and bury the rest
Shipped the top. Buried the rest.
My backlog is where features go to be outrun
estimates: I do not estimate, I deploy
jira: No Jira, no blockers, no problem
docs: Read the docs. Then shipped past them.
Docs read. Feature shipped. Same day.
I read the docs and shipped it twice

friday: Said no all week. Shipped on Friday.
No, no, no, and then a Friday deploy
Fridays are for shipping what survived
killed: Said no to my own feature. Loudly.
I say no. Sometimes to myself.
The feature I killed was mine
graveyard: My backlog is a graveyard and I dug every hole
I said no forty times. Here is the cemetery.
estimates: No to the feature. No to the estimate.
Asked for an estimate. Said no.
I do not estimate. I decline.
jira: Cannot say no to a ticket I never opened
Declined the invite. Declined the ticket.
docs: Read the docs so I could say no properly
I read it. The answer is still no.
An informed no. The best kind.

friday: Talked to users, shipped it that Friday
killed: Users told me. So I killed it.
Talked to five users. Killed my favourite.
The users were right. It is gone.
graveyard: Talked to users. Buried half the backlog.
Every grave in there was user approved
estimates: I estimate in interviews, not points
No estimates. I have user calls.
Ask the users, not the planning poker
jira: I talk to users. Jira talks to itself.
Never opened Jira. Opened forty user calls.
docs: I read the docs and I talked to a real user

friday: Shipped on Friday between two meetings
The Friday deploy happened during standup
killed: Killed my own feature. In a meeting.
It took nine meetings to kill my feature
I scheduled the meeting that killed it
graveyard: We discussed the backlog. Still a graveyard.
The backlog outlived the meeting series
estimates: I estimated it in a meeting. I was wrong.
Estimates are what I say in meetings
Committed to a date. In a meeting. Regrettably.
jira: Never opened Jira. In every meeting about it.
We meet about the board I have never seen
docs: I read the docs so the meeting could be shorter
The only one who read it before the meeting

friday: New here. Already shipping on Fridays.
Nobody told me not to ship on Fridays
Week three. Friday deploy. No supervision.
killed: Killed my first feature before it shipped
graveyard: The backlog was already a cemetery
estimates: New here. Already refusing to estimate.
Too new to estimate. Perfect excuse.
Nobody has asked me for a date yet
jira: Six weeks in, still have not opened Jira
New here. Jira remains a rumour.
Nobody has shown me Jira. Not asking.
docs: New here. Read everything. Suspicious already.
Read all the docs. Now I have questions.
New, and already the one who read it
